name: Kaohsiung International Airport
before:
Taiwan's second airport after Taoyuan, in Siaogang District on the south side of Kaohsiung. It handled 5.8 million passengers in 2024 and works from a single east to west runway with two terminals, one domestic and one international.

For getting around it is unusually well connected. The Kaohsiung Metro Red line has a station at the airport, which reaches the Taiwan Railway at Kaohsiung Main Station and the high speed rail at Zuoying. There is also a direct coach south to Fangliao and Kenting, which is the practical way to the southern beaches.

The airport was built as a Japanese army air base in 1942 and stayed military until 1965. International status followed in 1969 and regular international flights in 1972, though for two decades Hong Kong and Tokyo were the only destinations. The international terminal opened in 1997, and traffic has grown since 2009 on cross strait flights and low cost carriers.
after:
Kaohsiung's international airport, in Siaogang District on the south side of the city. It handled almost 7 million passengers in 2025 and works from a single east to west runway with two terminals, one domestic and one international.

For getting around it is unusually well connected. The airport has its own station on the Kaohsiung Metro Red line, which reaches the Taiwan Railway at Kaohsiung Main Station and the high speed rail at Zuoying. Coaches also run south to Fangliao and Kenting, the practical way to the southern beaches.

claims.note: Was 'Taiwan's second airport after Taoyuan'. The ranking rests on Wikipedia's 2024 figures alone: the Civil Aeronautics Administration's national table could not be reached (caa.gov.tw did not connect), so no rank is given.

claims.inAfter: It handled almost 7 million passengers in 2025
claims.note: Was '5.8 million passengers in 2024'. The airport's own operating-results table (linked from kol.kia.gov.tw as 高雄國際航空站營運實績 and hosted on ragic.com; read as a page and, for all rows, in its public data view) gives monthly passengers for domestic and international flights: the 24 rows for 2025 add up to 6,973,459 (international 5,741,629, domestic 1,231,830). Wikipedia's infobox, citing the Civil Aeronautics Administration, gives 6,971,162. CNA's report of 26 August 2026 quotes the aviation authority's director giving 5.74 million for 2025 and 3.96 million for January to July 2026: both match the table's international rows (5,741,629 and 3,956,194), so those are international passengers only and are not used for the total.

claims.why: Held back: verified but replaces nothing in the old text. CNA (26 August 2026) quotes the aviation authority: a new centralised terminal for 16.5 million passengers a year, built in two phases while the airport keeps running; CNA (16 July 2026) reports that after approval of phase one the taxiway move and car park works have begun, with the terminal building to follow once detailed design is done; Taiwan News (4 August 2026) lists a new terminal at Kaohsiung among the ministry's airport projects. Worth adding if Andy wants the works mentioned.
